newsitem.title: USA: NHL-FLYERS GRAB 2-0 SERIES LEAD WITH VICTORY IN BUFFALO.
newsitem.headline: NHL-FLYERS GRAB 2-0 SERIES LEAD WITH VICTORY IN BUFFALO.

text.p: The Philadelphia Flyers will take a two games to none lead back home with them after skating to a 2-1 victory over the Buffalo Sabres in their best-of-seven Eastern Conference semifinal series.
Garth Snow made 29 saves and Mikael Renberg and Chris Therien scored first-period goals for Philadelphia in the only NHL Stanley Cup playoff game played Monday.
Snow was at his best in the second period, when he stopped 12 shots. He faced only eight in the final period and was rarely tested as the Flyers dominated play.
"I don't know that they had many shots that were dangerous and not to many second shots," Snow said. "We controlled the game."

Renberg celebrated his 25th birthday by scoring his third playoff goal. Steve Shields made a glove save on John LeClair's slap shot from the top of the slot, but Renberg was left alone in front and swept a backhander into the open side of the net at 4:47.
While most teams are happy to come away with a split of the first two games of a playoff series on the road, Philadelphia was feeling greedy.
"We came here to win both games and we did it," Renberg said. "We can't let up now. I want to win it as soon as possible."
The Sabres had a golden opportunity to tie the game in the first period when Matthew Barnaby was alone in front of an open Philadelphia net but hit the crossbar.
What should have been a 1-1 game then became 2-0 for the Flyers when Therien got his first post-season tally with just over three minutes left in the period.
The Philadelphia defenceman put the puck through Shields's pads on a wraparound that looked like a replay of Shjon Podein's winning goal in Game One.
Buffalo's Jason Dawe broke up Snow's shutout with just 1:42 remaining in the second period to bring the crowd at the Marine Midland Arena to life.

Dawe was left unchecked at the right goalpost, and while Snow was watching another Sabre in front, Dawe took a pass from Dixon Ward and slipped the puck between into the open side of the Philadelpia goal.

Barnaby was frustrated again in the third period on one of Buffalo's best scoring chances. He tried a wraparound at the right goalpost with 9:22 to play, but Snow got his stick on it and the puck caromed to Derek Plante in the slot.
Snow managed to slide to his right and got his right shoulder on Plante's rebound attempt.

Shields, who finished with 35 saves playing in place of the suspended Dominik Hasek, kept Buffalo in the game down the stretch. He made a blocker save on a backhander by Eric Lindros on a breakaway with 4:27 left, then got his right skate on a backhander by LeClair less than two minutes later.
"Steve Shields was not a fault tonight," said Buffalo coach Ted Nolan.
Game Three is Wednesday in Philadelphia.
"We can and will play better. This isn't over," Nolan promised.
